assign.request: ext/editor adopts .panel-controls: one class per control-surface region so the hover bar stops covering first rows — the adoption the toolbar-edges task designed for.
assign.now: editor minion: class per control-surface region

action.msg: palette, layers and properties adopt .panel-controls on their region root; canvas, status and blank deliberately do not.

log.msg: Before, measured at 1600 with each bar lit: all five regions overlapped the bar by exactly 28.8px (--panel-bar-h = 1.8rem), body padding 0. After: palette, layers and properties measure overlap 0 (body padding 28.8px) and their first row hit-tests as itself, not .panel-bar. Zero console errors light and dark; /framework/ext/Panel/ untouched (1 control surface mounted, reserve 28.8px).

Three abstentions, on purpose. The canvas is the document, not chrome — reserving would inset the artifact from its panel and make the class mean 'every payload'. The status strip is a readout you glance at while the pointer is elsewhere, and it is a hug panel: 28.8px of reserve on a 36.45px strip nearly doubles it and takes the height out of the canvas. Blank's whole message points at the bar that covers it.

Flag, pre-existing and unchanged: the canvas's first block grip sits 13.3px under the lit bar (grip top 138.19, bar bottom 151.48) and elementFromPoint there returns .panel-bar, so the topmost block cannot be dragged by its grip while the bar is lit. Not a reserve problem — if it matters the fix belongs to the canvas's own top padding or the document layout, not .panel-controls.
Data safe: /data/editor.json and /data/editor-panels.json md5-identical before and after the whole verification run (selection is an id and never saves).

agent.outcome: landed — palette/layers/properties wear the class (overlap 28.8→0, first rows hit-test as themselves); canvas/status/blank abstain each for a stated reason; editor data md5-identical; console clean light+dark.
